title: La multa
goal: Talk your way out of a ticket, or find out what not doing so costs
culture: The transitero keeps your licence and you pay the ticket at a bank, not to him. Offering him money instead is a crime and a worse afternoon. Politeness is the only lever you actually have, and jefe plus an admission is most of it.

beats.es: Buenas. Su licencia, por favor. Se pasó el alto.
beats.objective: Greet him properly and admit it
beats.say: Buenas, jefe. No me di cuenta.
ok: buenas jefe no me di cuenta
buenas jefe no me di cuenta disculpe
beats.good: Jefe is respect without grovelling and no me di cuenta admits it without arguing. Both make the next minute cheaper.

beats.es: Es infracción, pues. Enséñeme la licencia y la circulación.
beats.objective: You have not got the licence on you
beats.en: I haven’t got my licence on me, boss.
beats.good: Ando sin... is not having it on you today, which is a smaller thing than no tengo. Andar is how Nicaragua says what you are carrying.

beats.es: Uh, peor. Entonces son quinientos, y los paga en el banco.
beats.good: Taking it is what keeps it at five hundred. There is no version of this conversation where arguing costs you less.

beats.es: Aquí le va el papel. Tiene ocho días para pagarlo.
beats.objective: Apologise for taking up his time
beats.good: Disculpe la molestia ends it on your terms. It is what you say to anybody whose day you took up, and it costs nothing.
